Lean Hog Futures Weekly Outlook - February 16–20, 2026

Top News Story: Managed Money Exits Bullish Bets as April Hogs Stabilize Following $6 Correction

The lean hog market spent the week of February 16 attempting to find a technical floor after the previous week’s aggressive $6.55 sell-off. While the front-month April contract set a life-of-contract high of $99.80 on February 4, the narrative has shifted from "supply panic" to "speculative reset." 

Managed funds, which held a massive net long position entering the month, continued their liquidation phase this week, though the pace of selling slowed mid-week as bargain hunters emerged. 

Supporting the market’s floor is the ongoing "protein substitution" play; despite the halt in Mexican cattle imports due to screwworm concerns in Texas, Choice boxed beef prices remains elevated near $365/cwt, keeping pork as the primary value feature for retail grocers.

Market Notes

The CME Lean Hog Index remains the primary source of bullish support, climbing another $0.40 to $87.59 (as of Feb 18), effectively narrowing the basis with futures. Cash trade showed signs of a mid-week bounce, with the national base hog price jumping nearly $3.00 on Tuesday to reach $88.23 before stabilizing. 

Pork carcass cutout values ended the week firm, priced at $96.28 on Thursday afternoon, a $0.72 gain. While belly and picnic primals showed slight weakness, a $4.41 surge in butt prices and firm ribs helped offset the losses. 

Thursday’s Export Sales report (delayed by the holiday) was neutral-to-soft, with net sales of 27,300 MT, down 5% from the previous week and 29% below the four-week average.

Price Summary and Recent Movements

After seven consecutive lower closes earlier in the month, April hogs saw a modest relief rally mid-week but remain under pressure from technical resistance at the 20-day moving average. Key CME data as of February 20, 2026:

Contract MonthLast Price (USD/cwt)Change (Day)Change (Week)VolumeOpen Interest

Apr 2026 (HEJ26)93.800+0.350 (+0.38%)+1.975 (+2.1%) Moderate 48,234
May 2026 (HEK26)97.000+0.700 (+0.70%)+0.950 (+1.0%) Moderate 3,410
June 2026 (HEM26)106.825+0.225 (+0.21%)-1.500 (-1.4%) Moderate 11,849
July 2026 (HEN26)108.400+0.150 (+0.14%) Modest Down Low N/A

Cash Trade: National daily direct base price volatile; Tuesday's spike to $88.23 was a high-water mark for the week.

Historical Context: April futures have successfully defended the 50-day moving average ($91.20), a critical "line in the sand" for bulls.

Key Market Factors
Supply: Q1 2026 pork production was raised 8 million lbs by USDA (to 7.1 billion lbs) due to heavier weights, but Q2 production was cut by 25 million lbs, suggesting a tightening summer supply.

Demand: Domestic demand is strong; export shipments are robust (37k MT) even if new sales have moderated to 27.3k MT.

External: Boxed Beef/Pork spread favors pork; Choice beef at $365.17 vs. Pork Cutout at $96.28.

Technicals: April hogs are testing resistance at the 10-day moving average (~$93.95). A break above this level could target a gap-fill toward $96.00.

Upcoming USDA Reports Expectations
With the Cattle on Feed report released Friday afternoon, traders will look for placement data to gauge how long the beef-driven demand for pork will last. No major hog-specific reports are due next week, but the market will be highly sensitive to the February 26 Weekly Export Sales, particularly seeking any renewed interest from China or the Philippines.

Funds Activity
The "Great Liquidation" of February appears to be tapering off. Managed money reduced their net long position significantly from the 143,000-contract peak seen earlier this month. As of the latest reporting cycle, funds still hold a sizeable net long, but the reduction has removed the "top-heavy" nature of the market. 

Open interest in the June contract is rising, suggesting funds are rolling positions forward rather than exiting the complex entirely.

Outlook for the Week Ahead
The market is entering a consolidation phase. The downside appears limited by the rising CME Index and the reduction in cattle imports, which creates a floor for all proteins. However, the lack of a fresh "bullish surprise" may keep April hogs capped at the $95.00 level in the near term. 

Key dates: Weekly Export Sales Feb 26.

Risks: A sudden drop in the cash index or a recovery in the U.S. Dollar that would hurt export competitiveness.

Strategy: Trade the $91.50–$95.00 range in April. Consider "buying the dips" near $92.00 as the summer supply tightening (Q2 production cuts) begins to be priced in.
#leanhogs #futures #markets #hogs
